request.title: Cataclysm 0.3 — mobile startup and strategic upgrades
request.prompt: Deliver an ACTUAL tested, published Cataclysm 0.3 core update to the existing docs/preview HTML5 survival game (not a document or proposal). Priority P0: GitHub issue #29 records real Samsung Android failure: the START RUN button did nothing. Investigate boot/version handshake, script loading, disabled button, event binding, cached game.js and runtime exceptions; fix demonstrated causes rather than guessing that joystick input is the culprit. If unavailable on hardware, make diagnostics visible and state physical-phone verification remains pending. Use issue #23 (Cataclysm 0.2 ~886-second gameplay review) for scope. After core startup/input is robust, deliver ONE meaningful 0.3 mechanic: on level-up offer 3 different player-selected upgrades (firing rate with hard cap, damage, movement speed); freeze simulation during choice, apply exactly the chosen upgrade, and resume cleanly. Preserve cat movement, automatic combat, fish, city, survival, health, waves, sound toggle, pause, replay, stable preview URL. Keep controls one-finger friendly; ensure arena gestures do not scroll the page while other page controls still work. Clarify HP/max-HP UI as far as achievable within this bounded run. Avoid broad new art/music/features. No external dependencies or services; only edit the allowlisted Cataclysm target files and coder report, not tests or workflows. Run Node syntax, focused game-specific test(s) of upgrade choice and reset, and the independent Playwright acceptance. Preserve read-only CATACLYSM_DIAGNOSTICS.snapshot() and extend only with copies of actual state for evidence. Rebuild/stamp cache-busting and visible Cataclysm 0.3 version through the publisher; do not claim real Samsung verification. If unable to satisfy the P0 and core acceptance, fail safely instead of publishing or weakening tests.
acceptance: A real tap on the existing #play button starts the game, hides #start-overlay, increments game time and allows actual player movement in both 390x844 and 360x780 touch-emulated browsers; no uncaught errors or missing resources.

Investigate and document the boot path, failed/disabled button risks, script-cache/version agreement and any observed root cause. Provide actionable on-screen initialization errors instead of silently leaving START RUN unusable; retain physical Samsung status as unverified.
Dragging on the arena moves the actual cat, pointercancel releases controls, and gameplay gestures do not scroll the document. Buttons and other page areas remain accessible.

An earned level-up opens exactly three selectable upgrades (fire rate, damage, movement speed). Simulation time and combat freeze during selection, choosing one changes only the corresponding stat, returns to running, and cannot be chosen repeatedly for the same level.
Firing rate upgrades have a bounded nonzero cooldown to avoid a runaway late-game attack exploit. Level and upgrade state reset on a new run.
HP versus max HP is accurately represented, damage does not create impossible heart values, and existing health, score, fish, kills, waves and auto-combat behavior stay functional.
Pause, resume, restart, death and replay work before and after using the new level-up interface. No fake scores or time progression are injected for tests.
Coder runs node --check, real focused gameplay/upgrade logic checks, and reports concrete results. Independent mobile browser acceptance and AI QA must approve actual source and evidence.
Display Cataclysm 0.3 build identity consistently, preserve the existing /preview/ URL and previous Git history; only publish if accepted source hashes match deployed bytes.

producer.claim: The job 'Cataclysm 0.3 — mobile startup and strategic upgrades' requires delivering a fully functional update to the existing Cataclysm HTML5 survival game featuring fixed startup reliability and one meaningful level-up mechanic with upgrades.
producer.rationale: The job's prompt and acceptance criteria specify that the START RUN button must reliably start the game on Samsung Android and other platforms, with detailed diagnostics on boot failures; player controls must be stable for touch and keyboard inputs; the game simulation must freeze during a level-up choice offering exactly three upgrades (fire rate, damage, movement speed), applying only the chosen upgrade with bounds to prevent firing rate exploits, and resuming correctly; the UI must accurately display HP versus max HP; existing gameplay features—combat, fish, city, health, waves, pause/resume, replay—must remain functional; and the build version must be clearly displayed with no external dependencies or broad new features added.
objections: Physical Samsung Android hardware verification remains unperformed due to environment limitations.
The level-up mechanic implementation may introduce new UI complexity requiring playtesting to ensure one-finger friendliness and no scroll interference.
Advanced corner cases around upgrade state reset and simultaneous input events may harbor subtle bugs without extended testing.
producer.proposed_action: Implement the requested update on the provided source files (index.html, game.js, game.css, game-config.json) strictly adhering to the job contract and acceptance criteria; include diagnostic messages visible on initialization failures; add the level-up mechanic with freeze-and-select upgrade UI; ensure proper input event handling for touch and keyboard; preserve all existing stable gameplay and UI elements; run Node syntax checks and focused gameplay tests on the new upgrade features; maintain cache busting and version stamping; prepare the coder report with test run results and any remaining risks; do not claim deployment or Samsung physical verification.
required_evidence: Successful Node syntax validation of game.js and related scripts post-edit.
Focused gameplay test logs demonstrating the working level-up mechanic: freezing simulation, upgrade selection, stat application, and resume.
Playwright acceptance test results confirming touch and keyboard controls start and run the game without errors, including behavior on emulated Samsung Android environment if available.
On-screen diagnostic outputs on boot/startup displayed if errors occur, with documentation of boot path and script/version handshake.
UI screenshots or video captures showing HP/max HP correctness, run state transitions (paused, running, dead), and the new upgrade choice interface.
Build version label correctly displayed matching released source hashes.

The HTML and CSS already display HUD elements, controls, overlays, and maintain a visible build version label. The acceptance criteria require freezing simulation on level-up to present exactly three upgrade choices (fire rate with capped cooldown, damage, movement speed) from which the player picks one, which modifies the corresponding stat only and is not repeatable for the same level.
objections: The existing version does not currently implement UI or logic to freeze simulation and present a selectable upgrade menu on level-up; adding it risks breaking the current steady behavior if not carefully integrated.
Physical Samsung Android device verification is beyond the environment scope and remains incomplete; diagnostic fallback prevents silent failures but real-device interaction is unverified.
Ensuring one-finger touch input remains smooth and page controls unbroken during the new upgrade selection UI requires careful gesture and event handling tests.
Edge cases in upgrade application and state reset on game restart might introduce inconsistencies requiring thorough gameplay testing.

The current code disables the START RUN button until the CATACLYSM_BOOT.ready() call from game.js executes with the correct build string; any modification here must preserve this handshake and error reporting to avoid regressions.
researcher.proposed_action: Implement the level-up upgrade mechanic as a modal upgrade selection UI triggered exactly when the player reaches the XP threshold and levels up; during this, freeze the game simulation and combat updates. The UI must present exactly three selectable upgrades: firing rate (with a hard minimum cooldown), damage, and movement speed. On selection, apply only the chosen stat increment, disallow repeated upgrades of the same type at the same level, then resume simulation. Preserve and enhance the START RUN button and boot/version handshake to display visible diagnostics for startup failures. Ensure one-finger friendly controls, no page scrolls during arena gestures, and consistent HP/max-HP display in the HUD. Update the build/version label as per current patterns and add cache busting. Run Node syntax checks on all edited files post-implementation, then focused game logic tests for the new upgrade mechanic to confirm freezing, choice, stat application, and reset on restart. designer.claim: The core loop must maintain continuous survival gameplay with automatic combat and enemy spawning, integrating a freeze-and-select level-up upgrade mechanic activated at XP thresholds. designer.rationale: The existing Cataclysm 0.2 canvas game provides automatic shooting, fish collection, enemy waves, and health with keyboard and touch drag control. The new core loop continues running game state only when mode is 'running'. Player movement velocity derives from normalized input vector combining keyboard and one-pointer drag deltas. The firing cooldown respects a hard minimum cooldown to prevent exploitation. A level-up triggers at the XP threshold, freezing game simulation/tick loop and combat processing. The three upgrades screen overlays above the arena and disables movement and input to the game until a selection is made. HUD updates dynamically with health showing hearts and empty hearts reflecting max HP vs current HP. Notices appear temporarily for damage or level-up events. The joystick UI matches one-finger drag location and movement vector, with fallback touch handlers for Samsung devices. Pause, resume, restart, and death screens integrate cleanly with this loop and mechanic. No external dependencies are introduced, and build/version labels are managed as before.

Ensuring upgrade state resets correctly on restart and disallowing repeated upgrades per level adds complexity where corner case bugs may arise without extended manual and automated tests.
The existing code handles the start button disable and boot/version handshake tightly; expanding diagnostics must avoid disrupting this delicate initialization sequence.

critic.claim: The current Cataclysm 0.3 update plan may fail to fully address concrete failure cases related to unresponsive start button, fake progress reports, comprehensive touch input handling, pause/restart edge cases, viewport overflow on small screens, upgrade balance enforcement, and prompt-mandated UI and diagnostic requirements.
critic.rationale: While the plan covers most requested features and diagnostics, it relies on emulated Samsung Android environments without physical hardware verification, which risks unaddressed device-specific pointer or touch event quirks causing unresponsive start or inconsistent input. The freeze-and-select upgrade mechanic adds complexity where input might still slip through or where simulation may partially advance, leading to 'fake progress' illusions. Pause and restart states interacting with level-up freeze state introduce corner cases prone to state inconsistencies or timing bugs. The current viewport and canvas scaling do not explicitly handle overflow or responsiveness on very small or unusual screen sizes, risking UI clipping or scroll bleed. Upgrade state reset and bounding cooldowns must be rigorously enforced to avoid runaway exploits or repeated upgrades per level. Although start button enablement and diagnostics are planned, real-world race conditions in boot/version handshaking and script caching conflicts might still silently disable controls or show stale UI, violating prompt expectations for visible actionable errors.
objections: Physical Samsung Android verification is pending, leaving success on real devices uncertain.
The freeze-and-upgrade UI implementation may allow inputs outside the intended modal or partial freezing of simulation, causing inconsistencies or fake progress.
Pause/resume during upgrade selection risks race conditions with game state transitions, especially if inputs overlap or if restart occurs mid-selection.
No explicit evidence is presented about viewport overflow handling or scroll prevention on various mobile device sizes beyond test viewports.
Upgrade application logic requires strict enforcement of cooldown floors and no repeated upgrade selection per level to meet balance requirements; implementation details may harbor corner case bugs.
Existing diagnostic code assumes synchronous, timely boot/version handshake, which may fail silently if script loading or caching encounters unexpected delays or errors.
One-finger touch controls coexist with page controls, but there is risk of accidental page scrolling during long drags outside the canvas area if event handling is not airtight.
critic.proposed_action:
1. Perform additional focused tests or static analysis to simulate physical Samsung Android input cases, ensuring fallback touch handlers fully prevent unresponsive start conditions and pointercancel events fire consistently.
2. Review the upgrade freeze state logic to guarantee no advancement of time, spawning, enemy movement or combat during upgrade UI display; formally verify that input events outside upgrade elements are ignored.
3. Add explicit pause/resume/restart test scenarios overlapping with upgrade UI active state to uncover potential race conditions, implementing state flags or locks as necessary.
4. Test viewport scaling and arena/canvas layout on smaller and irregular screen dimensions, confirming no viewport overflow or page scroll bleed during drag gestures; apply CSS or event handling fixes if needed.
5. Harden upgrade selection logic with guard clauses preventing repeated selection of same upgrade type for a level; confirm cooldown parameters respect specified hard caps.
6. Enhance diagnostic boot path with timeouts, status logs or visible messages for script caching/version mismatches or failures; ensure these disable start button and show retry instructions explicitly.
7. Audit and document event.preventDefault usage and touch-action CSS settings to fully suppress unwanted page scrolling during arena drag, preserving accessibility and other page controls outside the canvas.
8. Collect evidence from node syntax checks, automated gameplay tests on upgrade frozen state, Playwright acceptance runs on wide mobile viewports, and screenshots/videos showing correct HUD display including HP versus max-HP hearts, upgrade UI, and build version label consistency before publishing.

Focused gameplay test logs demonstrating that upon level-up XP threshold crossing, the game simulation fully freezes, the upgrade UI with exactly three options appears, only one upgrade can be chosen per level, and the simulation cleanly resumes with applied stats without any time or score inflation (fake progress).

Playwright-based acceptance test reports confirming that tapping the #play button reliably starts the game, overlay hides, player can move via touch drag, automatic firing works, no console errors occur, and pause/resume/restart work correctly on both 390x844 and 360x780 emulated mobile viewport browsers.

Viewport and gesture handling tests demonstrating no arena or joystick overflow, no page scroll during drag gestures inside the arena, and full access to other page controls.

coder_report:
# Cataclysm 0.3 core implementation

Status: implemented locally; NOT approved for publication. Browser acceptance could not launch in this sandbox. Physical Samsung verification and independent AI QA remain pending. No deployment or deployed-byte agreement is claimed.

## Scope and inspection

Read artifacts/mobile/job.json, plan.json and feedback.md (feedback was an empty array). Inspected the existing HTML boot handshake, disabled start button, event bindings, configuration loading, combat/pickup/level logic, pointer/touch fallback, diagnostics, styles, independent acceptance, and publisher stamp implementation before editing. No prior gate.log was present. Issue #29 and #23 context was supplied in the request; no live issue retrieval or hardware reproduction was available.

Only docs/preview/index.html, game.js, game.css and this report were edited. Existing config and publishing/test code remain unchanged. The /preview/ path is preserved.

## Changes and criteria

- Startup: retained real click-based START RUN / resume / replay bindings and readiness gating. HTML expects code 20261106-core-03; game.js acknowledges the same identity only after binding controls and exposing diagnostics. Script errors, runtime errors, rejected promises, version mismatch and initialization timeout now also put actionable reload/cache-clearing guidance inside the start overlay, adjacent to its disabled button, as well as in the existing page alert.
- Observed concrete defect: existing readiness code overwrote the publisher's label with hardcoded older run 42010567811. Corrected it to use the publisher's dataset.run. This demonstrates an identity bug, NOT the cause of the reported Samsung no-op; that root cause remains unverified. Missing/mismatched scripts and exceptions before readiness can leave START disabled by design, now with visible explanations. Existing per-script query was updated and publisher stamp supplies run-specific JS/CSS queries. Configuration fetch now uses cache: 'no-store'; replaced Object.hasOwn with the older-compatible prototype call.
- Level-up: actual collected fish reaching the existing XP threshold increments level and opens exactly three buttons: faster firing (cooldown ×0.85), damage (+0.25), movement speed (+18). Removed automatic mixed health/speed/damage gains and level-derived firing acceleration. Selection applies only its stat; guarded pending state rejects repeated clicks for that level. Earned XP is consumed, and simulation exits immediately into upgrade mode. Time, enemy movement, shooting, pickups and particle simulation freeze until a choice. Pause cannot bypass the choice; restart starts a clean running session during it.
- Fire rate: per-player interval has a hard 0.12-second floor at initialization, upgrades and firing. Level, XP, choices, stats, pointer/keyboard state, notice and overlay state reset on restart/replay.
- Health: numeric HP / MAX HUD and accessible descriptive label accurately show current versus maximum health. Death updates HUD immediately to 0 / 3. Health stays at its existing base maximum because the requested choices contain no health upgrade.
- Preserved original city, cat, auto-targeted combat, fish drops/magnet, score, kills, waves, survival/death, sound toggle, pause/resume, replay and local best behavior. Existing pointer capture, pointercancel and Samsung touch fallback remain; added lostpointercapture cleanup and centralized input release for transitions. Canvas/arena touch-action remains scoped to gameplay; page buttons remain native controls. Keyboard movement remains available even when a button has focus; Space/Enter activation on buttons is preserved. Reduced-motion preference suppresses screen shake and particle bursts.
- Diagnostics: CATACLYSM_DIAGNOSTICS remains frozen and read-only. Snapshots return copies of actual HP, stats, XP, level, choices, projectiles, enemies and input in addition to existing mode/time/position/build. No state-mutating diagnostic or fabricated progress added.

## Commands and results

- `node --check docs/preview/game.js`: PASS, repeated after final JS edit.
- `python game_factory/stamp_preview.py --directory /tmp/cat-stamp --run-id 42136897024-1`: PASS. Ran the existing publisher on a temporary copy of index.html and copied only stamped index.html back, to respect the allowlist prohibiting BUILD_INFO edits. Visible run is 42136897024-1; title displays Cataclysm 0.3; JS/CSS URLs carry the run ID. Final publishing/stamping and hash verification remain the runner's responsibility.
- `node /tmp/cat-focus.cjs`: PASS. Temporary Node VM harness loads actual final game.js with a stub DOM and in-memory-only test instrumentation inside its closure. It exercises real tick/pickup/threshold logic for each upgrade; verifies unchanged full snapshots across 100 frozen ticks, selected-stat-only change, duplicate rejection, copied diagnostics, resumed time, pause/resume, new-run reset. Also passes 120 earned firing upgrades reaching exactly 0.12 seconds, restart during a choice, contact-damage death and replay. It verifies exactly three HTML upgrade choices and stamped identity. It does not replace browser/physical tests; its controlled fixtures set fish/XP/enemy state only inside the temporary test context, never shipped code.
